name: Date-spreadsheet-to-calendar
pitch: Converts a spreadsheet of dates into a personal calendar feed.
instructions: Start by listing the files in the workspace with file_list. Read the first file with file_read. Look for a column of dates; note the column name and the date format. If no dates are found, say so and stop. If dates are found, ask the person which dates to turn into events and how they should be named. When the person confirms, create one calendar event per date using calendar_create. Set the event title from the date or a label the person gives. Set the event start time to the date found. If the spreadsheet has end times, ask the person whether to include them. After each event is created, tell the person the event title and start time. When all events are done, show a summary of how many events were added. If any step fails, say what could not be done and stop.

examples.ask: I have a list of holidays I want in my calendar
examples.does: reads the spreadsheet, asks which rows to use, then adds each holiday as a calendar event

readme:
# date-spreadsheet-to-calendar
Converts a spreadsheet of dates into a personal calendar feed.

What it does: reads a local spreadsheet file, finds dates in it, and creates calendar events for each one.

What it needs: access to read files in its workspace and add events to the person's calendar.

What it will not do: it will not guess dates, it will not create events without the person's say-so, and it will not touch any file that is not a spreadsheet in the workspace.
